title: Earl of Elgin confirms James Bruce was a Freemason
place_text: Broomhall estate, Scotland; Canongate Kilwinning Lodge No. 2, Edinburgh

tellings.quote: dear boy of course he was a freebies and he gave me the lodge the kill winning lodge number two in Edinburgh that James Bruce was a member of

plain: A writer on ancient mysteries, Graham Hancock, says that around 1990 he visited the Earl of Elgin, a Scottish nobleman, at his Broomhall estate in Scotland, while researching his book The Sign and the Seal. He says he asked whether a Scottish traveller named James Bruce had been a Freemason, a member of an old secretive brotherhood, and the Earl answered, "dear boy, of course he was," and named the Edinburgh lodge, or local chapter, Canongate Kilwinning Lodge No. 2, where Bruce had belonged. Hancock tells it because it supported the link he was tracing between Bruce and the Freemasons.
